subject: num.version error means JAGS may not be installed properly

messages.author: b92327f206542ca8
messages.subject: num.version error means JAGS may not be installed properly
parts:
Summary: the inscrutable error 'floor(num.version)' may indicate your
JAGS is incorrectly installed or not in your $PATH.

Working with someone to see if I could perhaps get access to a cluster
to run my model on (I estimate that with blavaan, it'll have a runtime
of ~10 days to get a decent sample of 10k), he tried to replicate my
basic data+model after installing JAGS and HEAD blavaan. Running my
model in 'bsem()', he got:

Found more than one class "Model" in cache; using the first, from
namespace 'lavaan'
Error in floor(num.version) :
non-numeric argument to mathematical function
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In blavaan(model = modelS, test = "none", data = scale(combined[-1]), :
blavaan WARNING: small sample drawn, proceed with caution.

2: In lavData(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label, :
lavaan WARNING: data argument has been coerced to a data.frame
3: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label =
group.label, :
lavaan WARNING: due to missing values, some pairwise
combinations have less than 10% coverage
Error in blavaan(model = modelS, test = "none", data =
scale(combined[-1]), :
blavaan ERROR: problem with jags estimation. The jags model and
data have been exported.
Calls: bsem -> eval -> eval -> blavaan

The call "floor(num.version)" appears nowhere in the blavaan source
code, the lavaan source code, the base R source code, or in Google, so
that was not helpful.
I confirmed he was running blavaan HEAD, R 3.3.0, and lavaan 0.5-20,
so it was not a version issue.
Testing the simple political-democracy example, that didn't work
either. Testing the political-democracy in lavaan, it did work. So it
was blavaan-specific.

The final traceback was

stop("blavaan ERROR: problem with jags estimation. The jags model
and data have been exported.")

Testing an example with 'run.jags()', the same error happened.
Finally, I suggested trying 'testjags()'. On my system

R> runjags::testjags()
You are using R version 3.3.0 (2016-05-03) on a unix machine, with
the X11 GUI
JAGS version 4.2.0 found successfully using the command '/usr/bin/jags'
The rjags package is installed

That gives normal output. On his system, that gave bad output.

It turned out that his JAGS had somehow not installed into his $PATH
and apparently, 'floor(num.version)' is how the JAGS executable not
being available expresses itself. I would have thought that runjags
would do an explicit check and return a better error message, but I
guess not. Once the path issue was fixed, 'bsem()' began running
without an issue.
